# Move Grantcoil exports to version 3

Grantcoil's v2 export API retires at **2031-04-15 00:00 UTC**. This advisory is for developers who maintain scheduled or interactive exports of arts-grant records. The replacement list endpoint is `/v3/grants`. Plan the change around the traversal model as well as the URL: version 3 supplies opaque cursors instead of page numbers.

## Understand the export boundary

A cursor holds a snapshot for 20 minutes from the initial request. A grant revoked after that snapshot was created remains in the current traversal. Start a fresh traversal to see the updated revocation status.

Each cursor belongs to one organization. Keep the organization's export context with the cursor so a saved continuation is not mistaken for an interchangeable page address. Use the cursor returned by the service; do not construct one from a page index or from a grant identifier. Replaying a cursor within its lifetime returns the same page and does not restart the snapshot lifetime.

The service sorts grants by increasing `awarded_at`. This gives the export a chronological progression rather than an order based on when a consumer happened to request each page. Treat this as the service's traversal order, not as an invitation to invent continuation values from the last timestamp seen.

## Adapt the page loop

The `page_size` default is 100 records, and the largest supported value is 250. Choose a size within that limit when adapting the consumer. Continue with each returned `next_cursor` until the field is absent. The final page omits `next_cursor`; it does not provide an empty-string continuation. A loop that checks only for an empty string would be using the wrong termination convention.

Keep the status filter attached to the traversal. Using an existing cursor with a different status filter produces `CURSOR_FILTER_MISMATCH`. If an operator changes the desired filter, begin a fresh traversal instead of combining the new filter with a saved cursor.

## Handle time and expiration

The `awarded_at` field uses ISO 8601 timestamps in UTC. Preserve that time interpretation in exported reports and comparison tools. Local display preferences should not be mistaken for a different ordering contract.

An expired cursor produces `CURSOR_EXPIRED` with HTTP status 410. Start a new traversal to recover. Because that traversal creates a new snapshot, do not describe the restart as a guaranteed continuation of the old result set. Changes in revocation status can make the newly observed records differ.

## Check deterministic ordering

Rows progress from earlier award timestamps to later ones, so the export follows award chronology across pages. When multiple rows have the same `awarded_at`, the service orders them by `grant_id` using ascending bytewise comparison. Retain that tie-break rule in migration notes: sorting tied identifiers according to a display locale would not describe the API's behavior.

## Explain the new behavior to report owners

A cursor holds a snapshot for 20 minutes from the initial request. A grant revoked after that snapshot was created remains in the current traversal. Start a fresh traversal to see the updated revocation status.

During handoff, distinguish a completed export from a restarted one. Report owners need to know whether the records came from one traversal or from a newly opened snapshot after expiration. Record the selected organization and status filter alongside the export context so the next maintainer can understand which request produced the report.
